title: Copilot Studio: conversational set-up of connector connections with in-chat sign-in
summary: Hold: the briefing describes licensing as unpublished even though Microsoft documents the product's access and licensing options. Distinguish those existing requirements from the narrower uncertainty about a separate charge for connection setup. The roadmap facts and the documented connection experience are supported.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: An agent needing an unset connection pauses and displays a Connection Required card.
claims.quote: When the agent needs a connection you haven't set up, it pauses and shows a Connection Required card.

claims.claim: The card's Set up connection button opens Manage your connections for the agent.

claims.claim: The card has a Retry button that tells the agent to try the action again after connection setup.
claims.quote: Retry | Tells the agent that you set up the connection, so it tries the action again.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Deny cancels the action and the agent does not retry it.
claims.quote: Deny | Cancels the action. The agent doesn't try the action again and tells you that it was canceled.

claims.claim: Users connect each item required by the action on Manage your connections and return to chat.
claims.quote:
On the Manage your connections page, connect each item that the action needs. Learn more in Connect an item.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Change & support
claims.claim: Connections are saved separately for each channel, requiring setup in each channel used.
claims.quote: Connections are saved for each agent and each channel. If you chat with the same agent in more than one channel, set up your connections in each channel.

claims.quote: In Microsoft Teams, the agent retries the action automatically after you connect. If it doesn't, or if you closed the dialog without connecting, select Retry on the card.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Tools configured for each user's account act through that user's connection, which the user manages.
claims.quote: Some tools in a Microsoft Copilot Studio agent sign in with each user's own account instead of one shared account. Before the agent can use one of these tools for you, you need to connect your account.

claims.claim: Create or pick connections lets the user select an existing connection or create one for each required service.
claims.quote: In the Create or pick connections dialog, for each service under Name, select an existing connection under Connection, or create a new one.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls

On the Manage your connections page, select the checkbox for each item you want to disconnect.

claims.claim: Disconnect cannot be undone.
claims.quote: The connections are removed for this agent in the channel where you chat with it, such as Microsoft Teams. You can't undo this action.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance

claims.claim: Stale means the agent changed after connection setup and the connection needs review.
claims.quote: Stale | The agent changed after you connected, so the connection needs to be reviewed. When you open the page, it tries once to restore the connection automatically.

claims.claim: The end-user connection article does not explain an unmet in-chat connection request when nobody is present to respond.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no licence is published for this feature.
claims.quote:
To use Copilot Studio, you need one of the following configurations:
- Copilot Studio user license (free).
- Copilot Studio authors role in Power Platform admin center.
- Microsoft 365 Copilot license
- Copilot Studio trial license.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to mixed and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing. Replace the blanket licensing absence in the notes, Cost and licensing, and cost rationale with: 'Copilot Studio documents access through a Copilot Studio user license requiring a tenant prepaid Copilot Credit pack subscription, the Copilot Studio authors role for applicable pay-as-you-go scenarios, a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, or a trial. The trial permits testing but not publishing. No separate entitlement for this connection experience is published.' Retain the distinct statement that a charge for the connection step itself is not stated.
